deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page (112r) is a draft from Riemann's Italian period (it mentions renewed leave and a salary increase granted from Göttingen). It belongs to the material published posthumously as 'Ueber das Verschwinden der Theta-Functionen' (Crelle 65, 1866). That page proves, by induction on m, a formula expressing a product Psi(z_1..z_m) Psi(zeta_1..zeta_m) through the m-th derivatives theta^{(m)}((r)), and concludes the following. If theta(r)=0, the 1st to n-th derivatives of theta(v) vanish at v=r, and the (n+1)-th do not all vanish, then the formula holds for m up to n but not for m=n+1. This page (112v) begins the summary 'Fassen wir das oben Bewiesene ... zusammen'. Several attempts are struck through or abandoned. In modern terms:

(1) Vanishing theorem. Let u_1..u_p be the normalized integrals of the first kind, with Riemann's additive normalization absorbing the Riemann constant. Write alpha_nu^mu = u_nu(eta_mu). Then theta(r_1,...,r_p)=0 if and only if there are p-1 points eta_1..eta_{p-1} with r_nu ≡ sum_{mu=1}^{p-1} alpha_nu^mu (nu=1..p), modulo periods. In modern language: Theta = W_{p-1} (+ kappa). The 'und umgekehrt' gives the converse: every such sum is a zero of theta.

(2) Struck-through first attempt at the refined statement: 'If m of these points eta can be chosen arbitrarily without changing r, and thereby the remaining p-1-m are determined, then ...'.

(3) Refined statement (singularity theorem), as rewritten. Suppose theta(r)=0, all partial derivatives of theta(v) of orders 1..m vanish at v=r, and those of order m+1 do not all vanish. Then m of the points eta may be chosen arbitrarily, and the remaining p-1-m are thereby determined. Conversely (unfinished sentence): if exactly m (and no more) of the points eta can be chosen freely without changing r, then [the derivatives up to order m vanish and not all of order m+1].

Modern form: mult_r(theta) = m+1 = h^0(D) = dim|D|+1, where D = eta_1+...+eta_{p-1} is the effective divisor of degree p-1 with r ≡ u(D). This is the Riemann singularity theorem.

No computation is performed on this page; it is a statement of results whose proof is on the preceding page.
errors: First line: Riemann first wrote 'p Punkte eta' and corrected it to p-1 (written above the line). Only p-1 points are correct.
The congruence holds only with Riemann's normalization of the u_nu, which includes the additive constant (the Riemann constant). It is modulo periods.

The converse of the refined statement is left unfinished. Strictly, the equivalence 'exactly m free points iff multiplicity m+1' needs the full argument with the m-th derivative formula from the previous page. As stated, it is correct (Riemann singularity theorem).
There are no mathematical errors beyond the draft slips.

results.what: theta(r)=0 iff r ≡ u(eta_1)+...+u(eta_{p-1}) for some p-1 points (with Riemann's normalization of constants)
results.modern_name: Riemann vanishing theorem (Theta divisor = W_{g-1} translated by the Riemann constant)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1857 Abelsche Functionen; 1866 'Ueber das Verschwinden der Theta-Functionen')

results.what: If theta and its derivatives up to order m vanish at r but not all of order m+1, then exactly m of the p-1 points eta can be chosen freely (dim|D| = m), and conversely
results.modern_name: Riemann singularity theorem: mult_r Theta = h^0(D) (generalized by Kempf 1973)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the summary of results published in Riemann's 'Ueber das Verschwinden der Theta-Functionen' (1866). Both the vanishing theorem and the multiplicity/singularity statement appear there and are credited to him. The page only documents the drafting.

checkable.asserts: Genus-1 case (p=1, empty sum of p-1=0 points): the suitably shifted theta (theta_1) vanishes at r ≡ 0.
Genus-1 case: the first derivative of theta_1 at its zero is nonzero, so the multiplicity is 1 = h^0 of the zero divisor (m=0, no free points), consistent with the singularity theorem.
Evenness of the theta function, theta(-v)=theta(v), which underlies the symmetry of the vanishing locus used in Riemann's argument.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: read 'Wenn theta(r_1, r_2 ... r_p) = 0 ist, so lassen sich p-1 Punkte eta so bestimmen, dass'. The 'p-1' is a correction written above the line, replacing 'p'.
Line 2: the congruence is (r_1, r_2, ..., r_p) ≡ (sum_{mu=1}^{p-1} alpha_1^mu, ..., sum alpha_p^mu). The '. Σ.' marks ellipsis dots between components.
Line 3: 'u_nu^*' is u_nu, with a correction mark over the index.

Refined statement: 'Wenn die ersten bis m^ten Derivirten der Function theta(v_1,...,v_p) für v_1=r_1, ..., v_p=r_p sämmtlich = 0 sind, die (m+1)^ten aber nicht sämmtlich = 0 sind, so können m [von den Punkten eta beliebig gewählt werden] und dadurch sind [die übrigen] bestimmt, und umgekehrt'. Words in brackets are left blank in the manuscript.
Last sentence (unfinished): 'Wenn m und nicht mehr von den Punkten eta, ohne dass sich die Grössen r ändern, beliebig gewählt werden können'.
